newsitem.title: GERMANY: Coalition, SPD positions in German tax talks.
newsitem.headline: Coalition, SPD positions in German tax talks.

text.p: Following is a bullet-point breakdown of position paper drafted by German coalition in response to demands put by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) before tax talks being held on Tuesday.
* Labour insurance charges: Coalition prepared to cut labour insurance charges by one percentage point from July of this year. SPD wants two-point cut, to be financed by petrol tax increase.

* Net tax cuts: Coalition says tax reforms will cut 30 billion marks a year in tax by 1999 -- not over 50 billion marks, as alleged by SPD. Coalition plans a one-point rise in value-added tax to partly offset direct tax cuts.
* Bringing forward tax cuts: Coalition ready to meet SPD demands for bigger tax cuts in 1998, but awaits proposals from SPD on how that can be financed.
* Tax allowances: Coalition rejects SPD demand to increase income tax allowance to 14,000 marks a year for single earners from 13,000 marks.
* Child benefits: Coalition rejects SPD demand to raise child allowances by 30 marks to 250 marks a month. Says measures to boost investment in jobs more important.
* Entry tax rate: Coalition wants to cut to 15 percent, in line with SPD demand for cut below 20 percent.
